name: application-masonry-grid
title: Masonry Grid
description: CSS-only variable-height grid using multi-column layout, so images or cards of different natural heights balance across columns without a JS layout engine — distinct from application-grids' uniform equal-height cells.
useWhen: Laying out images or cards with varying natural heights, like a photo gallery or a notes board.
You want a Pinterest-style balanced-column layout without pulling in a JS masonry library.
Content order top-to-bottom-then-across-columns is acceptable — CSS columns fill top to bottom within each column first.
avoidWhen: All items are the same height — use application-grids' uniform grid instead, it is simpler and gives more control over row alignment.
Reading order must go left-to-right, row by row — CSS multi-column layout flows top-to-bottom per column instead.
Items need to reflow or animate position on resize — CSS columns don't animate reflow the way a JS masonry library can.
responsiveBehavior: The columns count is a fixed prop; wrap the component in your own responsive class overrides (e.g. reduce to columns-2 or columns-1) to change the column count at narrower breakpoints.
accessibility: Every image carries descriptive alt text — decorative-only masonry galleries should still describe their content since users may rely on alt text to browse.
Card variant items use real heading (h3) and paragraph elements so their structure is available to assistive technology, not just visual columns.

variants.title: Image gallery
variants.description: CSS-only image masonry gallery where images of varying natural heights balance across columns.
accessibility: Each image carries alt text describing its content, not left empty.

variants.title: Image gallery (Dark)
variants.description: Image masonry gallery adapted for dark surfaces with a subtle ring per tile.
accessibility: The ring gives each tile a visible edge against the dark background where a shadow alone would not show.

variants.title: Card masonry
variants.description: CSS-only card masonry for content of varying length, such as notes or activity cards, using break-inside-avoid to keep each card intact.
accessibility: Each card uses a real heading and paragraph, not styled divs, so its structure is available to assistive technology.

variants.title: Card masonry (Dark)
variants.description: Card masonry adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Card border and text contrast must meet WCAG AA on dark backgrounds.
